item: The import's junk screen judges each article in one pass and reports read and judging time separately
summary: The prose gate tokenized each body three times, tested every token against every managed language's function-word set, and walked every character in Python to rule out an unsegmented script. It now tokenizes once, counts each language's hits from one tally of distinct tokens (same integers, same language order, same tie rule) and counts letters with C-level calls. Verdicts, densities and the script check are pinned against the previous implementation, kept verbatim in the test, on generated text in many scripts and languages including the nav-soup corner. Measured on 20,000 real-schema articles, warm cache: the whole screening went from 18.2-18.6 s to 7.1-7.3 s (about 2.5x); the gate alone 0.74 to 0.29 ms per article with a language and 2.5 to 0.79 ms without. The result now carries read_s and classify_s, so the next field run shows whether the 3,396 s was judging or reading the text off an encrypted store larger than RAM.
